17 / COMMON NEIGHBORS
V. COMMON NEIGHBORS

Recovery guarantees for CN

THEOREM 3.3POSITIVE RESULT

Common Neighbors achieves exact recovery w.h.p. if any of the following holds:

ALarge mean degree

Large mean degree rules out false positives, even for very small planted cliques.

BToo few common neighbors

Natural edges rarely have the small number of common neighbors required.

CToo many common neighbors required

The required number of common neighbors is too large for a natural edge.

Positive, sufficient conditions; depend on the dimension.

QUALITATIVE RECOVERY REGIMESLOG–LOG SCALES
A B C

Proof idea I: what can go wrong?

DECOMPOSING THE FAILURE EVENTTHREE BAD EVENTS
What could prevent the CN-algorithm from finding the planted clique?
No planted edge passes the algorithm.

Every planted edge has more than common neighbors, so none passes the exact-count test.

MISSED
PLANTED EDGE
A non-planted edge passes the clique test.

For some , all its common neighbors form a clique.

FALSE POSITIVE
CLIQUE TEST
A non-planted edge passes the count test.

For some , the number of common neighbors is exactly .

FALSE POSITIVE
COUNT TEST
An incorrect edge must pass both tests; controlling either false-positive event is enough.

V. COMMON NEIGHBORS

Proof idea II: finding a planted edge

FAR-APART PLANTED ENDPOINTSGEOMETRICALLY DISJOINT NEIGHBORHOODS

Added clique edges can connect spatially distant vertices.

WHY

Their natural neighborhoods cannot overlap.

Exactly the other clique vertices are common neighbors.

Uniform planted positions produce at least one sufficiently distant pair with high probability in the well-posed regime.

22 / COMPARISON
VI. COMPARISON & OUTLOOK

Numerical experiments

EXACT RECOVERY PROBABILITYμ = 12
VD Vertex Degree CN Common Neighbors HC Harmonic Centrality*
2D toroidal hard RGG · N ~ Poisson(10,000) · k = 2–40 · 1,000 realizations per point
HOW DO THE ALGORITHMS WORK?
VDVertex Degree

Select the k vertices with the highest degree.

Planting the clique increases their degrees; the algorithm relies on this increase standing out from natural degree fluctuations.

CNCommon Neighbors

For an edge (i, j), examine its common neighbors.

If there are exactly k − 2 and they form a clique, recover those vertices together with i and j.

HCHarmonic Centrality

Rank vertices by their global proximity to the rest of the network, using shortest-path distances.

Convention: . Select the k highest-scoring vertices.

Exploratory HC: 40 trials/point; exact for μ=4, approximate (256 reference vertices) for μ=12,36.
23 / NUMERICAL EXPERIMENTS
VI. COMPARISON & OUTLOOK

What have we learned?

01 STRUCTURE

Geometry changes the problem

Latent positions shape the graph and the limits of local recovery statistics.

02 ALGORITHMS

Common Neighbors can go further

Small planted cliques can be recoverable beyond the guarantees of Vertex Degree.

03 OPEN QUESTIONS

Beyond hard RGGs

Higher dimensions, soft connections, heterogeneous networks, and new centrality-based scores.

LOOKING AHEADFrom planted cliques to detecting hidden structure in realistic networks.
